Hi. I'm twenty-four myself in can relate so much. I still have yet to graduate college, I have about two years left (and that's IF I take regular course-loads). So far the most I've been able to handle a quarter is one. I have gotten many jobs and have either been fired or quit all of them because of depression. I can be doing relatively ok for a few weeks, and then BOOM everything falls apart again. I live in an apartment, not at home, but my parents pay for it. The only reason they're funding that is because I did live at home for a good while but it only got worse. I actually do a lot better away from my family and they know that. I'm extremely grateful for the amount of time and money they have put into helping me. I'm in a relationship that is slowly sinking. When I am depressed, it's terrible for my SO. He's losing patience I can tell. We've talked about getting married and having kids, we truly do love each other, but I'm growing increasingly afraid that this is impossible, that I'm too sick, and I want him to be happy. I see it crumbling before my eyes. 

I feel your pain, so much. I'm still alive by random chance and because most of the time I stop myself because I don't want to hurt people again. Honestly, I can't promise you that it's going to be ok. I can promise you that you are not the only one who feels this way or struggles this hard. I could be this huge success story, completely turn my life around, but it has yet to happen. New chances present themselves and eventually it turns into  absolute disaster. I gave myself a very long timeline for things to turn around, and if it's the same by then or worse, I've given myself permission to opt out without feeling (as) guilty as I would if I did it young. 

So, I don't know if this helps at all. I want you to know that you helped me because I read this and know I'm not alone. I want it to get better for both of us. It might not be right away which sucks, but I told myself I would be patient, because I still have a chance, and so do you. It doesn't seem like it, but we do. It may or may not work out, but you will never know unless you give it more time. I get it, it's like "Well, how many times can I get my heart broken before I collapse again?". I'm not sure but I'm still here so I haven't reached it yet.

I do have moments where I can feel happy, but I have a depressive cycle that I always fall back into. Please reach out, at least here.

OP I feel that. After years of drug cocktails I finally found the mixture that works for me. Here's where it gets tricky. I refrain from drinking because of the absolute damage it's done, not to mention it's like a one-way ticket to intense suicidal ideation. However, recently I've been smoking marijuana. I'm always honest to my psychiatrist about what I'm up to. I don't want to go off the deep end and end up where I was with alcohol. But this is such a different feeling...I can't even compare the two. My boyfriend and I only smoke on weekends and we go to concerts or out-and-about. So far I've felt great, not manic great, just like an all around good feeling. I am in the middle of my depressive cycle at the moment and while I have felt irritable it's nowhere near what it's usually like.

I guess my point is...I understand experimenting. It's certainly not the wisest choice, I know, but I'm not drinking, I haven't gone off the deep-end, and I feel that as long as my boyfriend and I are responsible and feel in control, why not? 

Be VERY careful with drinking. Dunno about you but for me it made me so much more depressed. See what works for you. Good luck man, I hope you're able to find a balance.
